name: Los Angeles
summary: A sprawling city of film studios, beaches, hills and world-class museums. Watch the sunset from Griffith Observatory, see the Getty's art and gardens, walk Venice Beach and Santa Monica Pier, and eat your way through the best tacos in the United States.
seasonNote: Mild all year. 'June gloom' brings grey mornings in early summer; September and October are warm and clear. Winter is cooler and occasionally rainy.
arrival: LAX is 30 to 90 minutes from most neighbourhoods depending on traffic; the FlyAway bus runs to Union Station.
gettingAround: LA is built for cars: rent one or use ride-hailing. The Metro rail links Downtown, Hollywood, Santa Monica and Universal City.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants.
foodTip: Tacos from trucks and stands, Korean barbecue in Koreatown, and In-N-Out burgers; Grand Central Market has everything under one roof.
buyTip: Vintage on Melrose Avenue, studio merchandise, and California wines.
baseArea: Santa Monica for beaches, West Hollywood for nightlife, Downtown for museums

items.name: Griffith Observatory
items.summary: An Art Deco observatory on a hilltop with free telescopes, a planetarium and views of the Hollywood Sign and the city.
items.expect: Parking is scarce at sunset; take the DASH bus.
items.tip: Hike up from the Fern Dell trail and stay for sunset and the city lights.
items.why: The best view in Los Angeles.
flow: Walk or take the bus up.
Exhibits, then the terraces at dusk.

items.name: Getty Center
items.summary: A hilltop campus of white travertine with European paintings, photography and gardens overlooking the city and ocean.
items.expect: Free entry; book a timed slot; parking is paid. Closed on Mondays.
items.tip: See the Central Garden and Van Gogh's Irises.
items.why: Great art, architecture and views in one.
flow: Tram up from the car park.

items.name: Santa Monica Pier and beach
items.summary: The classic pier with a Ferris wheel at the end of Route 66, and miles of beach on either side.
items.expect: Busy at weekends.
items.tip: Rent a bike and ride the beach path south to Venice.
items.why: The picture of Southern California.

items.name: Venice Beach and canals
items.summary: A boardwalk of street performers, Muscle Beach and skate parks, with quiet canals a block inland.
items.expect: Lively by day; best avoided late at night.
items.tip: Walk the canals, then Abbot Kinney Boulevard for shops and cafés.
items.why: LA's most colourful neighbourhood.

items.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
items.summary: The stars set in the pavement along Hollywood Boulevard, by the TCL Chinese Theatre's handprints.
items.expect: Touristy and crowded; costumed characters ask for tips.
items.tip: Go early and pair it with a studio tour.
items.why: The heart of the film legend.

items.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
items.summary: A working film studio and theme park, with the Studio Tour, Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World.
items.expect: Expensive; queues are long in summer.
items.tip: Do the Studio Tour first, then rides.
items.why: The most famous film studio tour.
flow: Rides on the upper and lower lots.

items.name: Disneyland
items.summary: Walt Disney's original 1955 park and California Adventure next door.
items.expect: Book tickets ahead; about an hour's drive.
items.tip: Use the Lightning Lane system for the biggest rides.
items.why: The first and most nostalgic Disney park.

items.name: Grand Central Market
items.summary: A 1917 food hall with tacos, egg sandwiches, ramen, oysters and pupusas.
items.expect: Busy at lunch.
items.tip: Try Eggslut's breakfast sandwich and Tacos Tumbras a Tomas.
items.why: LA's diversity on one counter.

items.name: Taco trucks and stands
items.summary: Street tacos al pastor, carne asada and birria from trucks across the city.
items.expect: Cash often preferred; best in the evening.
items.tip: Order al pastor carved from the spit and birria with consommé.
items.why: The best tacos north of Mexico.
flow: Find a truck with a queue.

items.name: In-N-Out Burger
items.summary: California's cult burger chain, with a short menu and a 'secret' one.
items.expect: Queues at peak times.
items.tip: Order a Double-Double 'animal style' with fries well done.
items.why: A Californian rite of passage.

name: Miami
tagline: Art Deco, beaches and Latin rhythm
summary: A city of pastel Art Deco hotels, white beaches and Cuban coffee, where Spanish is heard as often as English. Explore South Beach, the street art of Wynwood and the cafés of Little Havana, then head into the Everglades to see alligators.
seasonNote: December to April is dry and warm, with Art Basel in early December. Summer is hot, humid and stormy; hurricane season runs June to November.
arrival: Miami International Airport is 20 minutes from Downtown and 30 from South Beach; Fort Lauderdale is an alternative.
gettingAround: Ride-hailing is easiest; the free Metromover loops Downtown and Brickell, and Brightline trains run to Fort Lauderdale and Orlando.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; many restaurants add a service charge, so check the bill before tipping.
foodTip: Cuban sandwiches and cafecito from walk-up windows, stone crab in season (October to May), and Latin American food of every kind.
buyTip: Cigars in Little Havana, art in Wynwood and the Design District.
baseArea: South Beach for beaches and nightlife, Brickell or Downtown for the city

items.name: South Beach and the Art Deco District
items.summary: Ocean Drive's pastel 1930s hotels facing a wide white beach with candy-coloured lifeguard towers.
items.expect: Busy and loud on Ocean Drive; quieter on the side streets.
items.tip: Take the Art Deco walking tour from the Welcome Center.
items.why: The world's largest collection of Art Deco buildings.
flow: Walk Ocean Drive and Collins Avenue.

items.name: Wynwood Walls
items.summary: An outdoor museum of huge murals by street artists from around the world, in a district of galleries and breweries.
items.expect: Ticketed inside the Walls; the streets around are free.
items.tip: Walk the side streets for free murals.
items.why: One of the great street-art districts.

items.name: Little Havana and Calle Ocho
items.summary: The heart of Cuban Miami: domino players in Máximo Gómez Park, cigar rollers and cafecito windows.
items.expect: Lively on Friday evenings.
items.tip: Come on the last Friday of the month for Viernes Culturales.
items.why: Miami's Cuban soul.
flow: Walk Calle Ocho for coffee and cigars.

items.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
items.summary: A 1916 Italian-Renaissance-style villa on Biscayne Bay with formal gardens.
items.expect: Closed on Tuesdays; book online.
items.tip: Allow time for the gardens and the stone barge in the bay.
items.why: Miami's most elegant historic house.

items.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
items.summary: A museum of modern and contemporary art with hanging gardens on its bayfront terrace.
items.expect: Closed on Wednesdays.
items.tip: Have a drink on the terrace at sunset.
items.why: The architecture alone is worth it.

items.name: Everglades National Park
items.summary: The 'river of grass', with alligators, herons and a 24 km loop by tram or bike at Shark Valley.
items.expect: About an hour from Miami; bring water, sun cover and insect repellent.
items.tip: Rent a bike at Shark Valley and climb the observation tower.
items.why: A unique wetland wilderness.

items.name: Versailles Restaurant
items.summary: The world's most famous Cuban restaurant, open since 1971, with a walk-up coffee window.
items.expect: Mirrored dining room; busy late at night.
items.tip: Order a cafecito and croquetas at the window.
items.why: Cuban Miami's meeting place.

items.name: Joe's Stone Crab
items.summary: A 1913 South Beach institution serving stone crab claws with mustard sauce and key lime pie.
items.expect: No reservations at dinner; open mainly in crab season (October to May).
items.tip: Get takeaway from Joe's Take Away next door to skip the wait.
items.why: Miami's signature seafood.

items.name: Cuban ventanitas
items.summary: Walk-up windows serving cafecito, pastelitos and Cuban sandwiches all day.
items.expect: Quick and cheap; stand at the counter.
items.tip: Order a colada to share; it comes with tiny cups.
items.why: The daily ritual of Miami.

name: Orlando
tagline: Theme park capital of the world
summary: Home to Walt Disney World, Universal Orlando and SeaWorld, Orlando draws more visitors than almost any city in the United States. Beyond the parks are freshwater springs, the lakeside town of Winter Park, and the rockets of Kennedy Space Center on the coast.
seasonNote: Late January to early March and late October to early December have the shortest queues and mildest weather. Summer is hot with daily storms and big crowds; Christmas and spring break are peak.
arrival: Orlando International Airport is 25 minutes from Downtown and the parks; Brightline trains link the airport with Miami.
gettingAround: Rent a car or use ride-hailing; Disney runs buses, boats and a gondola between its resorts and parks.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work everywhere; parks are cashless in many places.
foodTip: Park food is pricey; Disney Springs and International Drive have hundreds of restaurants, and the Mills 50 district has the best Vietnamese food in Florida.
buyTip: Theme park merchandise and outlet malls on International Drive.
baseArea: Disney resort hotels for Disney, International Drive or Universal hotels for Universal

items.name: Magic Kingdom
items.summary: Disney World's classic park, with Cinderella Castle, Space Mountain and nightly fireworks.
items.expect: Book park reservations and Lightning Lanes ahead; huge crowds in holidays.
items.tip: Arrive 45 minutes before opening and stay for the fireworks.
items.why: The most visited theme park in the world.

items.name: EPCOT
items.summary: Disney's park of future technology and the World Showcase, with pavilions from 11 countries around a lake.
items.expect: Lots of walking; food and drink festivals for much of the year.
items.tip: Eat your way around the World Showcase in the evening.
items.why: The most grown-up Disney park.

items.name: Universal Orlando
items.summary: Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure and Epic Universe, with the Wizarding World of Harry Potter.
items.expect: Park-to-park tickets needed for the Hogwarts Express.
items.tip: Stay at a Premier hotel for free Express passes.
items.why: The best thrill rides in Orlando.

items.name: Kennedy Space Center
items.summary: NASA's launch site, with the Space Shuttle Atlantis, a Saturn V rocket and bus tours to the launch pads.
items.expect: About an hour's drive; check the launch schedule.
items.tip: Time your visit with a rocket launch from the viewing areas.
items.why: Where humans left for the Moon.
flow: Bus tour to the Saturn V centre.

items.name: Lake Eola Park
items.summary: Downtown Orlando's lake with swan boats, a fountain and a Sunday farmers' market.
items.expect: Relaxed; busiest on Sundays.
items.tip: Rent a swan boat and visit the Sunday market.
items.why: The real city beyond the parks.

items.name: Winter Park
items.summary: A leafy lakeside town with a scenic boat tour and the Morse Museum's Tiffany glass.
items.expect: Boutiques and cafés on Park Avenue.
items.tip: Take the Scenic Boat Tour through the canals, then the Morse Museum.
items.why: Old Florida charm.

items.name: Wekiwa Springs
items.summary: A spring-fed pool and river where you can swim and kayak among turtles.
items.expect: Fills up at weekends; arrive early.
items.tip: Kayak downriver in the morning.
items.why: Florida's crystal springs.

items.name: Disney Springs
items.summary: Disney's free-entry waterfront district with dozens of restaurants and shops.
items.expect: Busy in the evening; book popular restaurants.
items.tip: Free to enter and park.
items.why: The most choice near the parks.

items.name: Mills 50 Vietnamese
items.summary: A district of Vietnamese, Thai and Chinese restaurants northeast of Downtown.
items.expect: Casual and good value.
items.tip: Order pho and banh mi.
items.why: Orlando's best local food.
flow: Drive or ride to Mills Avenue.

items.name: EPCOT World Showcase dining
items.summary: Restaurants and kiosks from 11 countries around the EPCOT lagoon.
items.expect: Park ticket needed; book table-service meals ahead.
items.tip: Graze from kiosk to kiosk during a food festival.
items.why: A world tour of food in one evening.

name: Washington, D.C.
tagline: Monuments, free museums and the seat of power
summary: The US capital lines its National Mall with monuments and the free museums of the Smithsonian, from the Air and Space Museum to the National Museum of African American History and Culture. Walk from the Lincoln Memorial to the Capitol, then explore Georgetown and U Street.
seasonNote: Cherry blossoms peak in late March or early April, the busiest time. Summer is hot and humid; autumn is mild and clear.
arrival: Reagan National is on the Metro, 15 minutes from the Mall; Dulles is about 45 minutes by Metro Silver Line. Amtrak arrives at Union Station.
gettingAround: The Metro, buses and bikeshare cover the city; the Mall itself is best on foot or by bike.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work everywhere; the Smithsonian museums are free.
foodTip: Half-smokes at Ben's Chili Bowl, Ethiopian food around U Street, and the food halls of Union Market.
buyTip: Museum shops on the Mall, and Eastern Market on weekends.
baseArea: Downtown or Penn Quarter for the Mall, Dupont Circle for restaurants

items.name: Lincoln Memorial and the National Mall
items.summary: The great seated Lincoln looking down the Reflecting Pool to the Washington Monument and Capitol.
items.expect: Open around the clock and free.
items.tip: Walk the monuments at night when they are lit and quiet.
items.why: The most powerful view in the capital.
flow: Walk past the Vietnam and WWII memorials.

items.name: National Air and Space Museum
items.summary: The Wright Flyer, the Apollo 11 command module and the Spirit of St. Louis, in the Smithsonian's most visited museum.
items.expect: Free, but timed passes are required.
items.tip: Book free passes online ahead of time.
items.why: The story of flight in one building.

items.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
items.wiki: National Museum of African American History and Culture
items.summary: A moving museum tracing African American history from slavery to the present, in a bronze-latticed building.
items.expect: Free; timed passes often needed; allow half a day.
items.tip: Start at the bottom history galleries and work up.
items.why: One of the most powerful museums in the US.

items.name: United States Capitol
items.summary: The domed seat of Congress, with free guided tours of the Rotunda and Statuary Hall.
items.expect: Book a free tour; strict security.
items.tip: Walk through the tunnel to the Library of Congress next door.
items.why: The heart of American democracy.
flow: Tour, then the Library of Congress.

items.name: Library of Congress
items.summary: The world's largest library, with a gilded Great Hall and Main Reading Room.
items.expect: Free timed passes.
items.tip: Look down into the Main Reading Room from the gallery.
items.why: The most beautiful interior in Washington.

items.name: Georgetown
items.summary: A historic district of brick townhouses, the C&O Canal towpath and a riverfront park.
items.expect: Busy shopping streets at weekends.
items.tip: Walk the canal towpath and climb the 'Exorcist steps'.
items.why: The capital's oldest and prettiest neighbourhood.

items.name: Arlington National Cemetery
items.summary: The national military cemetery, with the Kennedy graves and the hourly changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
items.expect: Lots of walking; a tram tour is available.
items.tip: Time your visit for the changing of the guard.
items.why: A solemn place of national memory.

items.name: Ben's Chili Bowl
items.summary: A U Street landmark since 1958, famous for its chili-topped half-smoke sausage.
items.expect: Queues; open late.
items.tip: Order the original chili half-smoke with everything.
items.why: A Washington institution.

items.name: Union Market
items.summary: A food hall of local vendors, from oysters to Korean, tacos and ice cream.
items.expect: Busy at weekends.
items.tip: Go at weekend lunch and share several dishes.
items.why: The best food hall in Washington.

items.name: U Street Ethiopian restaurants
items.summary: Washington has one of the largest Ethiopian communities outside Africa, and its restaurants cluster around U Street.
items.expect: Eat with your hands from shared injera.
items.tip: Order a vegetarian combination platter and doro wat.
items.why: A flavour of DC you won't find elsewhere.

name: Chicago
summary: The birthplace of the skyscraper, set on the shore of Lake Michigan. Take the architecture river cruise, see the Art Institute's masterpieces, look up at Cloud Gate in Millennium Park, and argue about deep-dish versus tavern-style pizza.
seasonNote: Late spring to early autumn is glorious, with festivals and beaches. Winters are long and bitterly cold.
arrival: O'Hare is about 45 minutes from the Loop on the CTA Blue Line; Midway is 25 minutes on the Orange Line.
gettingAround: The 'L' trains and buses cover the city; Divvy bikes run along the lakefront trail.
cashTip: Cards and phone payments work everywhere.
foodTip: Deep-dish pizza, Chicago-style hot dogs (no ketchup), Italian beef sandwiches, and the restaurants of the West Loop.
buyTip: The Magnificent Mile for shopping, and architecture books from the Chicago Architecture Center.
baseArea: The Loop or River North for sights, West Loop for food

items.name: Millennium Park and Cloud Gate
items.summary: The mirrored 'Bean' sculpture, the Crown Fountain and free summer concerts at the Pritzker Pavilion.
items.expect: Busy; best early morning for photos.
items.tip: Come at sunrise for the Bean without crowds.
items.why: Chicago's front garden.

items.name: Chicago architecture river cruise
items.summary: A 75-minute boat tour along the Chicago River past a century of skyscrapers, with expert guides.
items.expect: Runs April to November; book ahead in summer.
items.tip: Take the Chicago Architecture Center's official cruise.
items.why: The best introduction to the city.
flow: Board at the Michigan Avenue bridge.

items.name: Art Institute of Chicago
items.summary: One of the world's great art museums, with Seurat, Hopper's Nighthawks and Grant Wood's American Gothic.
items.expect: Allow at least three hours.
items.tip: Start with the Impressionist galleries before the crowds.
items.why: Masterpieces on every floor.
flow: American art, then the Modern Wing.

items.name: Willis Tower Skydeck
items.summary: Glass boxes on the 103rd floor that let you stand over a 412 m drop.
items.expect: Queues at weekends.
items.tip: Go on a clear evening for sunset.
items.why: The most dizzying view in Chicago.

items.name: Lakefront Trail and Navy Pier
items.summary: A pier of rides, boats and summer fireworks on Lake Michigan, along a 29 km lakefront trail.
items.expect: Fireworks on summer evenings.
items.tip: Rent a bike and ride the lakefront to the beaches.
items.why: Chicago's lakeside playground.

items.name: Field Museum
items.summary: A natural history museum home to SUE, the most complete T. rex skeleton ever found.
items.expect: Allow half a day.
items.tip: Pair it with the Shedd Aquarium next door.
items.why: One of the world's great natural history museums.

items.name: Wrigley Field
items.summary: The Cubs' ivy-walled 1914 ballpark, one of the oldest in baseball.
items.expect: Season April to October; stadium tours year-round.
items.tip: Catch an afternoon game and a drink in Wrigleyville after.
items.why: A classic American ballpark experience.

items.name: Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
items.summary: A Chicago deep-dish institution with a buttery crust.
items.expect: Pizzas take 40 minutes; order ahead.
items.tip: Order the 'Malnati Chicago Classic' with sausage.
items.why: The classic deep dish.

items.name: Portillo's
items.summary: A local chain serving Chicago hot dogs, Italian beef and chocolate cake shakes.
items.expect: Fast and busy.
items.tip: Order an Italian beef 'dipped' with hot giardiniera.
items.why: Chicago's street food in one stop.

items.name: West Loop restaurants
items.summary: Randolph Street and Fulton Market's former meatpacking warehouses, now Chicago's best dining street.
items.expect: Book ahead for top restaurants.
items.tip: Walk Randolph Street's 'Restaurant Row' and pick one.
items.why: Where Chicago eats out.
